newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse seen flat or up slightly next week.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse seen flat or up slightly next week.

text.p: The Polish bourse has a chance to break out of its current sideways trend and achieve more significant growth next week, signalled by Friday's stronger buying after price fixing, analysts said.
"The strong buying after price fixing of some large-cap, fundamentally sound stocks signals there could be significant demand," said Czeslaw Pospieszynski of Bank Gdanski brokerage.
Analysts said a fall next week seemed unlikely and that one possibility was for gains on Monday and Tuesday, bringing in more buyers later in the week. @
They said the main market, currently at 13,670.3 points, could test 14,000 points.
The main WIG index inched up 0.8 percent this week.
Analysts said a possible negative signal hampering growth could be food prices for the second ten days of November due on Wednesday. Food prices rose 1.8 percent in the first 10 days.

"If food prices rise more than one percent it could have a negative effect on the market, but not too negative because people know prices tend to rise before the holidays," said Pawel Tarnowski of Raiffeisen Capital & Investment. @
Analysts said primary market offers of road builder GPRD SA, garment maker Elpo SA and construction firm Elektromontaz Warszawa SA could also draw money from stocks.
But they said a good sign was the prospective flow to the bourse of capital returned from the recent initial-public- offering oversubcription of Bank Ochrony Srodowisko SA.
Analysts said the week's top gainer garment maker Novita, up 7.8 percent, likely benefitted from recent better monthly earnings results.
They said computer maker Optimus, up 7.7 percent, had begun to benefit from the coming holiday season. @
But insurer Polisa fell 12.2 percent in the two days after opening 12.5 percent above issue.
Analysts said the firm looked fundamentally weak compared to the bourse's only other insurer Warta, which eased two percent this week.
NFI units rose 10.2 percent to 156.5 zlotys during the final week in which Poles may buy the certificates on the primary market. @

Analysts said the units could rise toward 200 zlotys over coming months, based on estimates of the assets of the 512 firms in the privatisation programme undergoing restructuring by international management firms.
